definitions: Relating to or denoting a dialect or accent of English in which the /r/ sound is pronounced after a vowel and before a consonant or at the end of a word (e.g., in 'car' or 'bird').
Characterized by the pronunciation of the /r/ sound in all positions where it was historically present.
examples: American English is generally a rhotic accent.
Many Irish accents are also rhotic.
The speaker used a rhotic pronunciation of 'park'.
